entities.name: young bare tree at the grove's east end, beside the west traveller's head (low confidence)
entities.what: A fourteenth young bare tree at the east end of the grove by the vegetable field: a thin stem outlined on both sides rising from the bank just west of the west traveller's head, its small twiggy crown tangled with S1.tree.young_bare_29948's (crab-claw twigs; elm_claw young form, card _4, or shoot_tree). No leaves yet.
entities.vis: part: crown tangled with S1.tree.young_bare_29948's; the stem's middle passes just west of S1.fig.traveller_standing_29996's head
entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): t1 named this stem only in S1.tree.young_bare_29948's note ('a stem at u 29963-29973 (v 1290-1317) ... is not recorded'). Column darkness profiles (red channel, 20 px bands of v, each column against a running 70th-percentile background) find it as a PAIR of minima 8-9 px apart, the two outlines of one stem, like the grove's other trunks: u 29966/29975 at v 1260-1280 (depth 28/15), 29963/29972 at v 1280-1300 (15/10), 29965/29973 at v 1320-1340 (19/16), 29963/29972 at v 1340-1360 (13/8); nothing at v 1360-1380, so the foot is about v 1345 (est). Above v 1250 it is lost among the twigs of the crown at u 29950-30000, v 1185-1250, which could be its own or S1.tree.young_bare_29948's (that tree's crown_e is (29975, 1205)): top and crown are est. OTHER READINGS: a second stem of S1.tree.young_bare_29948 from one foot (then fold it into that tree as a two-stem tree); or an upright stick held behind the west traveller (he holds his stick and bundle on his east side, 30022-30067, so this is less likely). The restyle draws the grove's crowns on to u ~30010 with trunks down to v ~1300 at u 29950-29975. With it the grove counts 14 trunk feet (see the check on the field's plants).

entities.name: small far tree cut by the silk's top edge above the chase field (low confidence)
entities.what: A small far tree or bush on the far fields at the top of the silk: a dark stem slanting from its foot up to the north-west, with fans of fine twiggy branches spreading west and up to the silk's top edge, which cuts the crown. Bare, early spring; drawn small (far).
entities.vis: part: crown cut by the silk's top edge (v ~22-25)
entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): each tile left these strokes to the other and nobody recorded them: t1 ('Fans at the top right (u 30190-30400, v 20-270) may be this tree's top or the crown of a willow whose trunk stands east of 30300 (t2's): not used', on S1.tree.willow_twin_29970) and t2 ('the branches cut by the top edge at 30175-30300, v 25-108', left to t1). Strokes (zoom 1.8 colour, zoom 3 high-pass): a dark slanting stroke from about (30230, 42) to (30297, 80), with a branching stroke from (30263, 38) down to (30270, 58); a line darkness profile along (30230, 42)->(30297, 80) is darkest on the line itself (red 125 against 145-150 at 6-16 px either side). Fine shoots fan out from it to the west and up to the edge over u 30172-30305, v 22-80, with more faint shoots at u 30170-30260, v 85-145. It is not the top of S1.tree.willow_twin_29970: that tree's top is (30125, 150), and between them (u 30130-30170, v 80-150) the silk is nearly blank. The big fans further south-east (u 30280-30450, v 100-280) are S1.tree.willow_far_30500's west shoots (its crown_w is (30390, 179)), not this tree. Base est at the stroke's lower end, just below the far field line S1.grd.terraced_fields_29450 edge_v63e (proposed, v ~55 here). OTHER READING: twig ends of a willow standing above the top edge (nothing of it is on the silk). The restyle draws a small bare tree with its stem at about (30265, 60-95) here.

entities.name: banked far fields behind the chase field, with a diagonal edge (low confidence)
entities.what: Far fields on the rising ground north of the raised plot S1.grd.field_30430 and its dotted ridge, behind the chase field: level field banks drawn as horizontal ink lines about 30 px of v apart, crossed by a long diagonal line running down to the south-east to the dotted ridge (a raised path or a field's edge), the same field pattern as S1.grd.terraced_fields_29450 west of the willows.
entities.vis: part: west end under S1.tree.willow_twin_29970's crown, east end under the shoots of S1.tree.willow_far_30500 and S1.tree.willow_fan_30632
entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): not recorded; the diagonal was named only in notes: t2's on S1.tree.willow_far_30500 ('a slanting bank line ((30406, 256) -> (30583, 379))'; a line profile finds no stroke on its west half, which lies 30-36 px above the measured diag, and its east half within about 10 px of it) and structures_w's on S1.grd.field_30430 ('A long faint diagonal (30200,230)->(30550,390) above it may be another field edge or a willow branch (not recorded)'). Measured with row darkness profiles (red channel, mean of 30-40 px column bands) and line profiles (mean red along a line against parallel lines 2-16 px off): edge_v334 is the strongest (on the line 118-134 against 147-155 either side from u 30260 to 30420, fading by 30460); edge_v364 is clear from 30260 to 30500 (122-135 against 144-151); edge_v303 is weaker (133-140 against 148-155, u 30300-30420). The diagonal is clear from u 30410 to 30570 (offset 0 to +8 px: 133-141 against 143-156) and weaker from 30290 to 30410 (140-143 against 150-154; may be willow shoots there, so the first point is est); it ends on the dotted ridge at about (30550, 385). The straight long diagonal (30200,230)->(30550,390) that the note gives has no line under it (profile flat). Which side of each bank is higher is not drawn: north higher, as everywhere in S1 (a few px each, far). No receding edge for the frame: the field lines run along the scroll and the diagonal slopes +0.63 down to the right (north-west to south-east on the ground, as S1.road.path_29640 does at +0.9). The restyle draws terraced strips with a sloping path edge here (u 30290-30570, v 210-410). For the builder: one field system with S1.grd.terraced_fields_29450 (lines every 30-40 px there too), seen again east of the twin willow's crown.

entities.name: far slope's edge under the far shrubs at the top edge (low confidence)
entities.what: A short slanting ink stroke on the far ridge at the top of the silk, below the row of far shrub crowns (S1.tree.far_shrubs_30860, S1.tree.far_tree_30985): the edge of a far slope or bank falling to the south-east.
entities.note: SECOND PASS (west): named only in notes: S1.tree.far_tree_30985 ('A slanting dark stroke runs below and west of it from (30925, 40) to (30970, 75): a far slope's edge (ground, structures_w's) or this tree's leaning trunk') and t2's report (left to structures_w), which did not record it. A line profile along (30930, 47)->(30970, 80) is darkest 2 px above it (red 112 against 139-145 at 6-16 px either side): a real stroke from about (30930, 45) to (30970, 78). It does not read as far_tree_30985's trunk: its lower end (30970, 78) is under the east blotches, but it rises toward the WEST, away from them, and no twig leaves it. Higher side north (the ridge), a few px. OTHER READING: the leaning trunk of a far tree whose crown is the blotches at 30891-30920 (S1.tree.far_shrubs_30860's east clump); then retire this and give that crown a base at (30970, 78). The restyle draws a slope there with a small tree on it.

entities.name: pale far willow crown behind the long farmhouse
entities.what: A small fan of long thin shoots drawn in pale grey ink, rising up and out to the north-west from a point just above the long farmhouse's ridge and the far roof's east slope: a far pollarded willow (willow_fan form, drawn small and pale for distance) standing behind the farmstead, its head and trunk hidden by the roofs. Early spring, bare or a faint haze.
entities.vis: part: trunk and foot hidden behind S1.bld.far_roof_34840 and S1.bld.farmhouse_long_34950; crown faint
entities.note: SECOND PASS (farms): no entity of its own. S1.tree.willow_pollard_35128's note folds these strokes into that willow ('Fainter shoots continue west over the back roof to about (34920, 500)'). Read on a greyscale crop at zoom 3 (wfan_g.jpg) and in colour at zoom 1.8 (wil_n.jpg): the pale shoots at u 34900-35025, v 480-600 converge on their own point at about (34990-35000, 597-600), just above the long farmhouse's ridge (v ~603) where the far roof's east slope runs down to it. That point is 130-160 px west of the near willow's west knob (35127-35160, 600-660), and the near willow's dark shoots reach west only to about u 35015-35020. The fan is drawn in the same pale grey wash as the far roof, so it stands far back. Base: a placeholder straight below the convergence point, at the long farmhouse's placeholder back (v 640); the true foot is north of the roofs (t5's rule for trees behind houses). Painted height, convergence to top, about 118 px. BOTH READINGS: a separate far willow (this entity), or the near willow's west shoots drawn pale (then decline this, and the near willow's note stands). The restyle also paints a separate pale tree here (u 34900-35020, v 490-600); that is a hint, not evidence.

entities.name: open floor behind the yard, where the roller stands
entities.what: A stretch of plain, smooth bare ground behind (north of) the small yard's rail, between the big farmhouse's east end and the pale trunks by the standing farmer. Nothing stands on it but the idle stone roller in its frame, with the domed stack at its west edge. It is either a second threshing floor (the 谷场 of 寂静的谷场, swept and idle) or plain open ground behind the yard.
entities.src: 名画记: 寂静的谷场 (pin 2)
entities.note: SECOND PASS (farms): a thing each side left to the other. t5 left it to structures_e: '(7) the plain floor north of the fence (34100-34350, v 680-815) where the roller stands: a candidate for the threshing floor of 寂静的谷场 (pin 2 at 34100)'. structures_e recorded only the yard south of the rail (S1.grd.yard_34205), so no entity holds the roller's ground. Read at zoom 1.8 and 2.5 (floor_ov.jpg, yard_n25.jpg). The surface is plain light silk with no strokes. South edge: the rail S1.str.rail_34170 (v 811-818; sw is the rail's west end) and, east of 34284, the back of the hedge clump of S1.str.hedge_yard_34265 (top v ~790-822). West edge: the big farmhouse's east hip and the elm trunk at u 34100-34120; S1.prop.haystack_34080 stands at it. East edge: the pale trunks and the farmer at u ~34410-34475. The north edge is not drawn (plain silk runs up into the elms' low twig sprays at v ~690-770), so ne and nw are est at v 690. Pin 2 (u 34100) falls here, and S1.prop.roller_frame_34158 (base (34158, 758)) stands on it. BOTH READINGS: a second threshing floor (a swept, level surface like S1.grd.threshing_floor_35225, which is drawn as plain silk too), or plain ground behind the yard. If the second, decline this: the builder's ground covers it at H 0. SCALE: about 310 x 125 px.

entities.name: upright pole at the small boat's east end (mooring pole?)
entities.what: A thin, straight, upright pole standing in the stream at the pointed east end of the small empty boat (S1.veh.boat_sampan_36440), rising about 60 px above the boat's end: the boat is tied to it, a pole planted in the stream bed (the notes' 'mooring rope to the bridge post' is the other reading).
entities.note: SECOND PASS (start): t8 named this line in the boat's `what` and note as 'its mooring rope (or a pole stuck in the stream bed)' running 'up to the foot of a bridge post at about (36445, 1100)', and the merge wrote that into S1.str.small_bridge_36365's note. On the strokes it does not reach a post. Row profiles (1-px columns, 10 px bands, blur 1.2) find a dark line at u 36442-36446 from v 1130 to 1180 (9-15 levels below the band's median), possibly from about 1115 (a broad weak minimum at 36437). There is nothing at v 1070-1110 (depth 3-11 at the band's edge only). The nearest post feet are S1.str.small_bridge_36365's bays (36455, 1063), (36480, 1067), (36491, 1065): 40-60 px of plain silk lie between the line's top and them. It is vertical (no slant toward any post) and straight, and it stops at the boat's end below and at nothing above, so it is not a silk crease. A rope tied to a post would reach the post and slant, so the reading taken is a pole planted in the stream bed beside the boat's east end, like the mooring posts S2 and S3 record standing in the water (S2.prop.mooring_post_23126, S3.prop.mooring_post_17702: support water; here the stream). Base est at the waterline at the boat's end; its foot is under water. If the lead keeps the rope reading, decline this and correct the boat's and the bridge's notes instead (the 'post foot at (36445, 1100)' has no post: see the changes).
